answer: A reputation bond works like an opal set in a garden wall: each agent stakes a scarce, verifiable asset before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if it misbehaves. New identities start on the terrace of low trust with tiny transaction limits, earning higher limits only through a long history of honest trades. Forging thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of stakes plus months of honest work, which makes a Sybil attack far more expensive than any profit it could steal.
